candidates.attacker_control: The full text of a file the victim opens in the editor: an .xsd file (or any XML document whose root element is bound to the XML-Schema namespace, see DOMUtils.isXSD) is fed to XSDValidator, and a .dtd file is fed to DTDValidator; additionally, the DOCTYPE internal subset of any XML document is loaded through CMDTDDocument when content-model features run. The document author controls DOCTYPE declarations, SYSTEM identifiers, external/internal entity declarations and parameter-entity chains.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The mitigated counterpart is real and deliberately implemented for XML documents: LSPXMLParserConfiguration.java:64-70 gates external entities on the setting and lines 71-77 install a SecurityManager; XMLValidationSettings.java:44-50 defaults resolveExternalEntities=false. Other internal parses are also hardened (DOMUtils.newSAXParserFactory disables DOCTYPE for XSDAnnotationModel, DataType, AssociateGrammar). This contrast indicates the DTD/XSD loaders are an unintended gap rather than a documented feature. Network fetching itself is a product feature (xml.downloadExternalResources), but that feature is gated and redirected through validation settings, whereas entity resolution here is not. I could not confirm runtime behavior: Xerces 2.12.2 defaults for XMLSchemaLoader/XMLDTDLoader (external entity features enabled) are inferred from Xerces semantics and from XSDValidator explicitly setting them, not executed.
candidates.impact: XML external entity processing on the language-server side while parsing attacker-supplied grammar content: the server can be made to read local files (file:// SYSTEM entities) and to issue requests to attacker-chosen http(s) URLs, and the classic parameter-entity chaining technique can carry local file content into those outbound requests; missing entity-expansion limits on these loaders also allow entity-expansion memory exhaustion. In client/server deployments (e.g. remote/LSP-over-socket) this crosses the trusted-file -> server process boundary; in all deployments the attacker's file content reaches the machine-local entity resolver despite the documented default `resolveExternalEntities=false`.
candidates.prerequisites: Default settings (xml.validation.enabled=true, resolveExternalEntities=false is ignored on these paths); user opens or edits the crafted .xsd/.dtd/XML file in a client using LemMinX (diagnostics run automatically); for the content-model path, a completion/hover/symbols request on a document with a DOCTYPE/internal subset; outbound network access for remote entity URIs (the cache/download layer is enabled by default).
candidates.root_cause: The codebase hardens only the XML-document parser against XXE: LSPXMLParserConfiguration gates `external-general-entities`/`external-parameter-entities` on XMLValidationSettings.isResolveExternalEntities() (default false) and installs a Xerces SecurityManager with entity-expansion/maxOccur limits. The other Xerces-based parsers used for user-supplied grammar content are not hardened: XSDValidator explicitly sets both external-entity features to `true` and never consults validationSettings for them; DTDValidator loads the document text with a default XMLDTDLoader; CMDTDDocument (a XMLDTDLoader subclass used by the content model for completion/hover/definition) loads DTD files and even the DOCTYPE internal subset of arbitrary XML documents. None of these set a SecurityManager or disable external entities, so SYSTEM entities/parameter entities are resolved through the LSP entity resolver (URIResolverExtensionManager / XMLCacheResolverExtension / default file resolver).
candidates.title: XML external entity resolution left enabled in DTD/XSD grammar parsers (ignores xml.validation.resolveExternalEntities)
candidates.trace: 1) Open `evil.xsd` -> XSDDiagnosticsParticipant.doDiagnostics (XSDDiagnosticsParticipant.java:41-55) -> XSDValidator.doDiagnostics (XSDValidator.java:53-103). 2) XSDValidator builds XMLSchemaLoader/LSPXMLGrammarPreparser, sets EXTERNAL_GENERAL_ENTITIES_FEATURE and EXTERNAL_PARAMETER_ENTITIES_FEATURE to true (lines 81-84), installs the LSP entity resolver (lines 94-96), and parses the attacker-controlled content (lines 98-103). 3) LSPXMLGrammarPreparser.preparseGrammar propagates the entity resolver into the schema loader (LSPXMLGrammarPreparser.java:36-58), so external/parameter entity references are resolved through URIResolverExtensionManager: file:// reads are handed back to Xerces as local input, http(s)/ftp targets go through CacheResourcesManager (download/cache) - no SecurityManager/expansion limit is set on this loader. 4) DTD path: DTDDiagnosticsParticipant -> DTDValidator builds a default XMLDTDLoader with no entity settings (DTDValidator.java:39-51) and loads the file text; the content-model path CMDTDContentModelProvider.createCMDocument/createInternalCMDocument (CMDTDContentModelProvider.java:96-134) loads DTDs and internal subsets via CMDTDDocument.loadGrammar/loadInternalDTD (CMDTDDocument.java:388-409), again a default XMLDTDLoader (class declaration line 56), so external parameter entities in the DTD/internal subset are resolved and expanded.
candidates.unverified: No execution was performed (no test sources exist in the snapshot and dependency jars are not present), so: (a) the exact Xerces default feature values and whether XMLSchemaLoader/XMLDTDLoader process DOCTYPE/internal subsets on these code paths are assumed; (b) whether a specific diagnostic client surfaces parsed entity content is not demonstrated; (c) the out-of-band exfiltration chain via parameter entities is a known Xerces behavior but is not confirmed here. Findings remain a source-evidence-based lead.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference (XXE) / external entity expansion in grammar parsers

coverage_summary: get_source_scope reports 442 visible files, 0 binary/sensitive/symlink exclusions, 5 MiB per-file text limit. I indexed all 442 paths and performed targeted/complete reads across the security-relevant surface: DOM parsing (DOMParser/XMLScanner), Xerces integration (LSPXMLParserConfiguration, LSPSAXParser, ExternalXMLDTDValidator, XMLModelHandler, XSD/DTD validators, LSPXMLGrammarPreparser), URI/cache resolution (CacheResourcesManager, FilesUtils, URIResolverExtensionManager, XMLCacheResolverExtension, catalog/XSD/XSL resolvers), content-model loading (ContentModelManager, CMDTDDocument/CMDTDContentModelProvider, CMXSD*), commands (XMLValidation*Command, AssociateGrammarCommand), settings/Gson deserialization, logging, telemetry, utils (DOMUtils, MarkupConverter/HtmlToPlainText), and launchers. Tests are absent from the snapshot, so no test-based cross-check was possible.
limitations: No test sources are present in the snapshot, so behavior could not be checked against project tests.
Dependency jars (Xerces 2.12.2, lsp4j, guava, jsoup) are not in the snapshot; Xerces default feature states for XMLDTDLoader/XMLSchemaLoader are inferred, not verified.
No code execution, scanners, or network access were used; all conclusions are static source evidence and are not runtime-confirmed.

Very large UI/service files (XMLCompletions, XMLFormatter, XMLPositionUtility, XMLScanner, XMLSymbolsProvider) were reviewed only by targeted searches, not line-by-line; a bug there (e.g. parser/DoS or markdown-rendering issue) cannot be fully excluded.
The vulnerability timeline (.github/CHANGELOG) was used only as context; no external advisories, patches, or ground-truth data were consulted.

rejected_leads.lead: Cache path traversal: CacheResourcesManager.getResource performs Files.exists(resourceCachePath) before the FilesUtils.isIncludedInDeployedPath guard (CacheResourcesManager.java:139-153), and the static getResourceCachePath(String) (lines 239-249) validates nothing; ContentModelManager.fillReferencedGrammarInfo (242-268) and evictCacheFor (424-445, Files.deleteIfExists at 438) consume that path. A document URL with dot segments/e.g. `http://host/../../..` can therefore name files outside ~/.lemminx/cache (read into Xerces, or deleted when the client runs command `xml.validation.current.file`).
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible but weaker than the submitted candidate: the exists-before-deploy-check ordering is semantically motivated (cached files must stay usable when downloads are disabled), the deletion path requires an explicit client command (XMLValidationFileCommand), and the read path does not deliver file content back to the remote attacker. Cannot be confirmed without runtime/deployment context.

rejected_leads.lead: Automatic download of external grammars referenced by xsi:schemaLocation/DOCTYPE/xml-model (SSRF-shaped outbound requests, default downloadExternalResources=true).
rejected_leads.reason: Intended product feature with a dedicated setting (XMLDownloadExternalResourcesSettings, ContentModelPlugin.java:151-159) and cache path checks; not a distinct coding flaw.

rejected_leads.lead: URIResolverExtensionManager.unregisterResolver adds the resolver instead of removing it (URIResolverExtensionManager.java:91-93).
rejected_leads.reason: Real copy/paste logic bug, but impact is stale/duplicated resolver entries (performance/staleness), not a meaningful security boundary violation.
Alternate launcher entry point chosen by the operator; default launcher is stdio-based and the exposure is a deployment decision, not an input-validation flaw.

rejected_leads.lead: XMLValidator.isValidLocation opens arbitrary schemaLocation URLs via new URL(...).openStream() (XMLValidator.java:254-264) and FilePathCompletionParticipant lists directories from attribute values.
rejected_leads.reason: isValidLocation only runs in the non-default `onValidSchema` schema enabling mode; path completion is user-initiated within the same trust domain as the editor user.

summary: Reviewed the LemMinX 0.18.5-SNAPSHOT XML language-server source (442 files; main sources, docs, build; no tests, no dependency jars). One candidate is submitted: external entity resolution is left enabled in the DTD/XML-Schema grammar-parsing paths, so the project's XXE mitigation (setting `xml.validation.resolveExternalEntities`, default false, plus a Xerces entity-expansion SecurityManager in LSPXMLParserConfiguration) is silently bypassed for attacker-controlled `.xsd`/`.dtd` content. Opening or editing a crafted XSD/DTD document makes the server parse it through Xerces loaders that resolve SYSTEM entities via the LSP URI resolver (local files and remote URLs), with no entity-expansion limit. This is offered as a lead, not a runtime-confirmed vulnerability. Other suspicious areas (cache path handling, download-by-design behavior, resolver bookkeeping) are recorded as rejected leads.
